text:
jessica: Heads up — prod canary failed on `inference-worker` upgrade. Helm error: "rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists and is not managed by Helm: PodDisruptionBudget \"inference-worker-pdb\""
omar: ugh. That usually means the rendered name is static and collides with an existing resource. Any chance the pdb name is hardcoded?
jessica: here's the pdb template from chart/templates/pdb.yaml:
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: inference-worker-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference-worker
```
leah: yep — no `{{ include "fullname" . }}` or release scoping. If an older manual PDB exists, helm will refuse to adopt it.
omar: not just manual — our GitOps pipeline renders charts with `helm template --name-template {{ .Chart.Name }}` in the renderer stage, which strips release scoping we rely on for uniqueness. So two different releases can render the same `inference-worker-pdb` name.
jessica: interesting. Locally `helm lint` passes (no cluster check) and `helm template` we run in CI differs from the GitOps renderer. I didn't catch this earlier.
sre-rotations: deploy-bot noticed the canary in prod hit the PDB collision and rolled back the canary. It logged:
```
deploy-bot: rollback triggered: upgrade failed: rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists and is not managed by Helm: PodDisruptionBudget "inference-worker-pdb"
```
omar: two fixes: 1) make the PDB include release/chart scope in name so it's unique; 2) add a lint rule in our chart-checker CI to forbid bare/static names for cluster-local resources.
leah: agreed. Proposed change to template:
```yaml
metadata:
  name: {{ include "fullname" . }}-pdb
  labels:
    app: {{ include "name" . }}
```
jessica: patch ready in draft MR. Also noticed values.schema.json for the chart has `properties.selector` typed as `object` and our `values.yaml` sometimes sets selector to "" in overlays, leading to rendering `matchLabels: ""` in some environments. That was causing weird kube api validation earlier too.
omar: oh that's classic env-drift: overlay sets empty-string to remove a map, but JSON schema expects object. We should allow `null` or use `anyOf` in schema: `[ {"type":"object"}, {"type":"null"} ]`.
leah: or change templates to `with` guard: `{{- with .Values.pdb.selector }} selector: {{ toYaml . | nindent 8 }} {{- end }}` so empty/false doesn't render a broken selector.
sre-rotations: also add a small CI job that runs `helm template` using the same flags as GitOps renderer and validate names with a quick grep for `-pdb` occurrences to assert uniqueness per release. The current mismatch between local/CI/GitOps caused the blind spot.
jessica: +1. MR will: update pdb name to `{{ include "fullname" . }}-pdb`, wrap selector rendering with `with`, update values.schema.json to allow null, and add a new lint job `chart-gitops-render-check` that runs `helm template --name-template {{ .Chart.Name }} --include-crds` and fails if any resource has a static name matching a known blacklist (pdb, svcaccount, clusterrolebinding).
omar: tiny nit — prefer to add a chart helper `template "uniqueName"` to centralize naming so we don't forget in future templates.
leah: also add a short note in chart README about GitOps renderer semantics and why release-scoped names are important. Newcomers keep using plain names.
deploy-bot: queued: `chart-lint/eng-platform/inference-worker` will run the MR checks.
jessica: thanks team. Will push the MR and tag everyone for review.
omar: after merge, let's run a one-off k8s check in prod to see if the old manual pdb exists; if so we'll either delete it (if safe) or adopt by renaming our new one.
leah: if manual pdb owned some manual eviction policy, coordinate with oncall. Use `kubectl get pdb inference-worker-pdb -n prod -o yaml` to inspect owner refs.
sre-rotations: noted — oncall will be pinged if the MR touches prod resources. :thumbsup:
